newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares flag but two trades fatten turnover.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares flag but two trades fatten turnover.

text.p: Prices slumped to a new six month low on Monday but a pair of cross deals in cotton and cement shares fattened turnover on the Cairo stock exchange.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index, which closed lower all last week, shed 6.53 points to 334.51 points -- its lowest level since January 19 when it closed at 330.01.

Of the 94 shares traded, 53 ended lower and 19 rose. Turnover was a deceptively high, above average 85.7 million pounds ($25 million), swollen by two share crossings in Nile Cotton Ginning and Amriyah Cement.
The CMA said the Nile Cotton Ginning trade was 31.2 million pounds and Amriyah Cement deal amounted to 20.4 million.
One broker said they comprised one trade of 588,000 shares in Nile Cotton and one move of 200,000 shares in Amriyah Cement. A total of 256,597 shares changed hands in the cement firm, the CMA said.
"There was a kind of crossing being done between two brokerages in which certificates of ownership were being transferred," said Rasha Lashin, floor broker for EFG Hermes.
She said the one movement in Amriyah was executed at 79 pounds. The share closed down 1.15 pounds to 80.
"It's the same point with Nile Cotton Ginning. There was a crossing of one transaction of 588,000 shares," Lashin said.
The ginning's share price rose one to close at 54 pounds as 611,300 shares changed hands in seven trades.
"The market saw approximately 35 million actual turnover," Lashin said. Traders have said individual investors have either given up on the market or were on their summer holidays.
Egyptian Portland Tora Cement, Suez Cement and Helwan Portland Cement all closed lower in unremarkable trade.
"There was nothing very much of interest. Prices are going down in the housing sector also," Lashin said.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development fell 10.4 pounds to 214.65 and Heliopolis Housing and Development was down six to 410, both in light trade.
"CIB was highly demanded but down," she said of Commercial International Bank/CIB, which closed 1.1 pounds lower at 69.01.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 447.97 points from 462.65 points on Sunday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms also slipped to 250.14 points from 253.4.
